commands.review_summary:
The PR centralizes review-artifact validation, adds phase-aware PR lock release and a `ci-dispatch` command, and adds a dependency-less-worktree guard to `scripts/committer`.

PR surface: Tests +388, Docs 0, Other +530. Total +918 across 18 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source: force `enter_worktree` to fail after beginning a review checkout and observe that the supervisor still sees validation rather than side effects, allowing the lock to release.

target.title: chore(pr): landing-UX — aggregated validation, lock classes, ci-dispatch, committer guard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Seven consecutive PR landings on 2026-07-18 surfaced four recurring frictions in the `scripts/pr` flow, each hit multiple times: artifact validation rejects one field per run (three fix-revalidate-recover cycles for one PR), the operation lock demands manual token recovery even for trivial schema rejections that spawned nothing (~8 recoveries), the "Missing successful recent CI workflow" failure names the symptom but not the non-obvious release-gate dispatch recovery, and `scripts/committer` in a dependency-less worktree fails mid-flow after argument processing — once allowing a chained push of an incomplete branch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Four bounded fixes, one PR:

1. **Validate everything at once.** `scripts/pr-lib/review-artifacts.mjs` now owns a single-source enum table used both to generate templates (with allowed values embedded as placeholders, so they cannot drift) and to validate; `review-validate-artifacts` aggregates every violation and ends with `N artifact violations`.
2. **Lock classification.** A monotonic `unannounced → validation → side-effects` phase notification over the existing supervisor FD: ordinary validation failures (exit 1–127 before any side effect) auto-release the operation lock; anything after the first mutation, signals, detached work, or drain failures retain it with the existing token recovery.
3. **Actionable CI recovery.** The hosted-gate failure now prints the recovery, and a new `scripts/pr ci-dispatch <PR>` resolves the remote head and dispatches the exact-SHA release-gate run, polling briefly for the run URL (`observed_run_url`, honestly labeled; `pending` when indexing lags). Fork PRs are rejected fail-closed (fork branches cannot be base-repo dispatch refs).
4. **Committer worktree guard.** Dependency-less-worktree detection runs before staging anything, and an explicit `--no-verify-formatted` flag supports the documented bypass — no auto-fallback without asserted formatting proof.

## User Impact

Maintainer/agent tooling only: fewer landing round-trips, no lock ceremony for typo-class failures, self-explanatory CI recovery, and committer can no longer half-fail after mutating state.

## Evidence

- Suites (all passing): review-artifact validation 5, ci-dispatch 5, operation-lock classification 5, prepare-gates 38, wrappers 8, committer 10.
- Black-box: an invalid artifact fixture prints all three violations plus the summary and exits 1; a valid one exits 0. Committer rejection leaves HEAD and index untouched; the explicit flag commits.
- `bash -n` across `scripts/pr`, `scripts/pr-lib/*.sh`, `scripts/committer`; node syntax checks; `git diff --check` clean.
- Autoreview (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`) clean, no actionable findings.
- Dogfood: this PR was committed in a dependency-less worktree via the new `--no-verify-formatted` flag, and its CI was dispatched with the new `ci-dispatch` subcommand.
- `test/scripts/oxlint-boundary-guards.test.ts` fails in this worktree with the diff stashed and passes on current `main` in the primary checkout — environmental (no worktree node_modules), not a regression.

Release-note context: `chore: smoother PR landing tooling — aggregated artifact validation, smarter lock recovery, ci-dispatch subcommand, committer worktree guard`.
